newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - S.Electric H1 profits to slip.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - S.Electric H1 profits to slip.

text.p: British regional electricity company (Rec) Southern Electric, twice thwarted in merger plans, should see a slip in half year profits when it reports on November 28 and will be expected to outline its future plans.
"The question really is, what are they going to do now?" said one analyst on Friday who asked not to be identified.
Southern Electric is expected to turn in half-year pretax profits of between 102 and 120 million stg, down from 127.8 million stg previously as a price review which bit in April weighs in.
It should pay out an interim dividend of 11.3 to 12.6 pence per share, up from 10.5 pence previously.

"The results will show the impact of the price review and then we will want to see its development strategy now it has been squeezed into standing on its own," said the analyst. In April, the government stumped Southern Electric's plans to link up with generator National Power by blocking the 2.5 billion stg agreed bid for the Rec.
Then in June, it threw in the towel in a bid war for its local water company against Scottish Power, which paid 1.68 billion stg to take control of Southern Water.
"I think we will see a little bit of both, some return to shareholders and some expansion plans," said the analyst.
Southern Electric might choose to pay out a special dividend rather than buy back shares because recent tax changes have made the latter option less attractive, analysts said.
But "it is very unlikely that Southern will return all of its balance sheet strength to shareholders," the analyst said.
"Southern has shown it is not averse to takeovers and it may be considering other options," he added.
